_comment: Building catalog for the settlement build menu. category: 'resource' (ticks a resource), 'housing' (the old per-species recruit gate -- every such entry is locked, and the gate itself is gone; Barracks capacity is the gate now), 'functional' (unlocks an action button), or 'main' (the player's home -- auto-placed at game start, not buildable, not removable, has hp and is the Crusade's target). 'requires' is another building_id that must already exist in the settlement before this one appears in the build menu (empty string = always available). Costs: Bone Pile/Dark Altar cost the resource they themselves refine (Bones/Dark Essence); everything else is ordinary construction and costs Wood/Stone, the resources Workers gather (see WorkerSystem.gd) -- Dark Essence stays a separate ritual/magic resource, not a construction material.
_comment_barracks: The Barracks is category 'housing_intake' -- a category of exactly one, and deliberately not 'housing' (that category means the old per-species hard gate, now locked). It is the recruit intake building per FOUNDATION_SPEC section 9: 'capacity' residents, 'unique': true so only one can ever exist (BuildingCatalog.buildable_ids drops it from the menu once placed), and no 'requires' -- GAME_OUTLINE Stage 2 puts the Barracks *first*, before the Workshop tech line, so gating it behind the Workshop would invert the intended build order. Its Upgrade button exists in the Barracks panel but is hard-locked, per the same section.
_comment_house: 'recruit_house' (category 'housing_home') is the home a recruit builds for themselves once you fund it -- flat 6 wood / 4 stone, charged by the fund-a-house action rather than by this entry, which is why 'cost' is empty. It is 'locked' because the player never places one from the build menu: the RECRUIT picks the cell, by their race's housing_style (see HousePlanner.gd and RACES.md). Its sprite_path is the default; the actual sprite and tint are overridden per race at placement time so a goblin warren and a minotaur's lodge don't look identical.
_comment_description: 'description' is the one-line 'what is this for' shown by the InspectionPanel when the player clicks the building on the map. It lives here rather than in a Dictionary in GDScript for the same reason costs and prerequisites do: adding a building should be a data edit, never a new branch in a description function. Keep it to one sentence or two -- the panel wraps it at ~300px.
_comment_locked: 'locked': true keeps an entry in the catalog but out of the build menu -- BuildingCatalog.buildable_ids() filters it. Used by the Stage-1-3 foundation reset (docs/history/2026-07-foundation-reset.md) for the five old per-species housing buildings (superseded by the Barracks-intake + fund-a-house model in FOUNDATION_SPEC section 9 and the housing_style rules in RACES.md). They are deliberately NOT deleted: Building.gd still reads their housing_species field, and these entries are the reference for whatever replaces them. 'blueprint': true is the other gate (LIVING_WORLD L2, 2026-09-26): the entry shows only once its blueprint is known in the meta profile -- the Dark Altar, whose blueprint is inside the first wolf den.

bone_pile.description: A heap of gathered bone, sorted and stacked. Yields a slow trickle of Bones with nobody tending it.

dark_altar.description: Where the dead are made stronger than they were. A living sacrifice buys a Ghoul (level 2) -- the living come later.
dark_altar._comment_altar: LIVING_WORLD L2 (2026-09-26): blueprint-gated, not locked. Its blueprint is inside the first wolf den (section 3) and is known for good once found. The legacy passive Dark Essence tick is gone -- essence is field loot only (LOOT_SITES_SPEC section 5). Its job is Summon Ghoul (ROGUELITE_REWORK 17.5), which needs a living prisoner (LIVING_WORLD L3).

bone_crypt.description: Stacked stone niches for skeletal labour that needs no roof, only somewhere to be put.

charnel_pit.description: A pit kept deliberately foul. Ghouls prefer it that way.

haunted_spire.description: A thin tower of black stone. Wraiths roost in the upper dark.

war_camp.description: Hide tents and a fire that never quite goes out. Orcs sleep within reach of their weapons.

burrow_warren.description: A hillside riddled with tunnels. Goblins pack in far tighter than looks survivable.

workshop.description: Benches, tools, and someone who knows the use of them. Unlocks the Blacksmith line.

blacksmith.description: Forge and anvil. Turns Dark Essence into gear for your followers.

barracks.description: Where new arrivals sleep until you fund them a house of their own. No Barracks, no recruits.

cell.description: Iron rings in a stone floor and a door that locks from outside. Holds 4 prisoners. They eat: one food each, dawn and dusk.
cell._comment_cell: LIVING_WORLD L3 (section 10.4, ruling 6): prisoners need a building and they eat. A blueprint like any other -- the first prisoner he searches knows how one is built (data/captives.json). 'capacity' is prisoners held, read by Captives.cell_capacity().

recruit_house.description: A home a recruit built for themselves once you paid for the timber. Frees their Barracks slot.

throne_of_bones.description: Your seat, raised from the dead of a hundred battlefields. If it falls, so do you.
